land.text: Gurgen's kingdom: 'Gurgen died in 1008, leaving his throne for Bagrat'

predecessors.note: Bagrat III inherited the Bagratid throne of the Iberians from Gurgen in 1008 (Cliopatria's row ends 999).

land.text: 'In 978, the aristocracy invited Bagrat to claim the throne of Abkhazia'

predecessors.note: The Abkhazian kingdom has no Cliopatria row; its dossier is not written (see report).

land.text: the Kartli rump: 'Major disintegration of the Georgian kingdom dates from 1463 with the defeat of George VIII at the Battle of Chikhori'

successors.note: The kingdom-of-kartli dossier starts in 1478 and carries Cliopatria's Kingdom of Georgia shapes of 1478-1578 and 1706-1762; Cliopatria's own Kingdom of Kartli shape of 1463-1467 (130 k km2, the whole old footprint) is marked wrong there.

land.text: western Georgia: 'In 1484 ... Alexander proclaimed himself king of Imereti (Western Georgia)'
Kakheti (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Kakheti row starts in 1468)

successors.note: The Kartli page mentions George VIII's 1465 defeat and capture but not his Kakheti title date.

capitals.name: Tbilisi

capitals.name: Kutaisi
capitals.note: 'Queen Rusudan had to evacuate Tbilisi for Kutaisi' during the 1236-1243 conquest; the page gives no year.

capitals.name: Tbilisi
capitals.note: Infobox 'Tbilisi (c. 1122-1490)'; under the Mongols the eastern kings sat in the Mongol-protected capital (George V page: 'ruled from Tiflis as Viceroy and ally of the Il-Khan'). Timur sacked it in 1386 and Jahan Shah in 1440.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1010 but the page unifies Georgia under Bagrat III c. 1008 ('Gurgen died in 1008, leaving his throne for Bagrat'); Kakheti-Hereti is annexed only in 1010 and Tbilisi 'remained in Byzantine and Arab control', so both are taken out of the 1010 outline.

correction.text: the 1010 outline without Tbilisi (Arab control); Kakheti-Hereti inside after its annexation in 1010

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1010-1013 inside the 1010 shape: 'Bagrat ... annexed [Kakheti-Hereti] in 1010', so it stays in; Tbilisi was still 'in Byzantine and Arab control' and is removed. From 1014 the 1010 verdict below applies.

correction.text: the 1010 outline without Kakheti-Hereti (independent from George I's first year) and without Tbilisi

keyframe_review.note: No area figure on the page (infobox: map caption only), so the Cliopatria area is not compared. 89.6 k km2 is about all of modern Georgia plus Zaqatala and Sheki. George I 'recognized the independence of Kakheti' in an agreement 'that deprived Georgia of more than a third of its territory within the first year of his reign' (1014; Kvirike III took 'King of Kakheti and Hereti'), and Kakheti-Hereti stayed apart until David IV took it in 1104. Tbilisi was Muslim until 1122. Stands for 1014-1022 only; from 1023 the new keyframe 1023 also takes out Javakheti (the 40-km circle of the 1023 loss is drawable; the earlier remark that the gazetteer cannot split it from Samtskhe was wrong). [Repair run 2026-10-31.]

union.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

correction.text: the 1010 outline without Kakheti-Hereti, Tbilisi and, from 1023, Javakheti, which George I ceded to Basil II

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1023-1045 inside the 1010 shape. Basil II page: 'George agreed to a treaty that handed over Tao, Phasiane, Kola, Artaan and Javakheti' (the sentence has no year; the page puts Basil's final offensive in early 1022, the treaty is dated 1022-23 on George I's page). Javakheti is the only one of those districts inside Cliopatria's outline. The Javakheti page says only that it 'suffered greatly from the invasions of Alp Arslan in 1064' and 'remained in the hands of the unified Georgian monarchy' in later centuries; the Bagrat IV page (opened 2026-10-31) does not mention it. Cliopatria's own 1085-1098 shape lacks it and the 1099 shape has it again, so it stays out until 1098 (ledger 1099, confidence 1).

union.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

correction.text: the 1046 outline without Kakheti-Hereti and Tbilisi and, since the 1023 treaty, without Javakheti

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 1010 (89.4 k km2) and the same correction: Kakheti-Hereti independent and Tbilisi Muslim. The page has Bagrat IV 'vacate Kakheti and retreat to Kartli' in 1068 under Alp Arslan, which hints at Georgian presence in Kakheti but dates no annexation before David IV's in 1104 (David IV page). Javakheti (ceded 1023, Basil II page) is subtracted as well; it is back inside only in Cliopatria's 1099 shape. [Repair run 2026-10-31.]

union.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

correction.text: the 1072 outline without Kakheti-Hereti and Tbilisi and, since the 1023 treaty, without Javakheti

keyframe_review.note: Same correction as 1046. 'from 1079/80 onward, George was pressured into submitting to Malik-Shah ... at the price of an annual tribute': the shape is drawn direct while the tribute lasts (the Seljuk dossier carries the suzerainty). Javakheti (ceded 1023, Basil II page) is subtracted as well; it is back inside only in Cliopatria's 1099 shape. [Repair run 2026-10-31.]

No area figure on the page (infobox: map caption only), so the Cliopatria area is not compared. 20.2 k km2 holds only Abkhazia, Samegrelo, Svaneti and Racha and has no Kutaisi, which agrees with 'Since 1080, when the emir Ahmed captured Kutaisi' (George II then accepted Seljuk suzerainty and tribute) and 'the Seljuq garrisons occupied the key fortresses in Georgia's south' (Seljuk wars page). This shape also lacks Javakheti, which agrees with the 1023 cession and the 1064 Seljuk invasion. [Repair run 2026-10-31.]

61.2 k km2 adds Imereti and most of Kartli. The pages date only that David IV stopped paying tribute to the Seljuks in 1099 and that Tbilisi and Rustavi stayed Turkish until 1122 and 1115; no page dates the recovery of Kutaisi or Kartli, so the shape stands but is early or late by an unknown number of years. Javakheti is inside this shape again (new ledger entry 1099, confidence 1: no page dates its return). [Repair run 2026-10-31.]

71.4 k km2 now holds all Kakheti (annexed 1104 per the page) and Kartli without Tbilisi; Rustavi follows in 1115, Lori and Agarak in 1118, Tbilisi in February 1122. Trialeti 1110 and Botora (February 1120) are defensive victories.

No area figure on the page (infobox: map caption only), so the Cliopatria area is not compared. 197.4 k km2, the maximum: Tbilisi (1122), Ani and northern Armenia (1124), Shirvan to the Caspian ('Georgia extended from the Black Sea to the Caspian Sea', 1123 on the David IV page). Stands for 1126-1129; from 1130 Demetrius gives up Ani and eastern Shirvan (new keyframe 1130).

correction.text: the 1139 outline applied from 1130: Ani and eastern Shirvan outside, vassal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1130-1138 inside the 1126 shape: 'the Christian part [of Shirvan] was incorporated into Georgia and the border being the Tetritsqali' (1129-30) while Manuchihr became emir of eastern Shirvan under Georgian vassalage, and 'Demetrius had to ... give up Ani to the Shaddadids on terms of vassalage' (1130). Cliopatria's 1139 outline already shows that, nine years later. [Repair run 2026-10-31: the two 1130 losses (Shirvan east of the Tetritsqali, 19 k km2; Ani) now precede the vassal entries. They explain about 24 k of the 49 k km2 by which the 1139 outline is smaller than the 1126 one; the rest of that difference lies in central Armenia and the Aras side, where the only page sentence is the 1130 Shah-Armens attempt 'to oust Georgians from northern and central Armenia', and no page names the land surrendered. Listed as a gap.]

148.0 k km2: the post-1130 settlement (Shirvan to the Tetritsqali, Ani a Shaddadid vassal). Demetrius 'raided the city of Ganja in Arran' in 1139 without annexing it ('in 1143 the town again fell to the sultan').
144.6 k km2, unchanged. 'In 1161, George III took over Ani': Ani flips in and out of the outline (1161, 1164, 1174, 1199) with no Cliopatria change.

144.3 k km2. 'On 9 July 1163 Seljuks inflicted a heavy defeat on Georgians', 'In April, 1164 Georgians evacuated the town [Ani]', 'in 1174 King George captured the Shahanshah ibn Mahmud ... and captured Ani once again'; the outline does not follow these swings.

144.3 k km2. 'Early in the 1190s, the Georgian government began to interfere in the affairs of the Eldiguzids and of the Shirvanshahs ... reducing Shirvan to a tributary state'; Shamkor (1195) moved no border.

144.4 k km2. 'Around the year 1199, a Georgian army under Zakare's command took the city of Ani from Shadaddid control' and 'in 1201, Tamar gave it to him as a fief': Ani was already inside the outline.
159.6 k km2 (+15 k): 'In 1206, the Georgian army, under the command of David Soslan, captured Kars and other fortresses' (the Kars district enters the outline), after the Dvin gains of 1203-1205.

191.1 k km2 (+31 k), all inside Georgia, Armenia, Turkey and Azerbaijan, none in Iran. The page dates the 1209 Khlat siege and the Ardabil-Marand-Tabriz raid but no annexation; the added land is not explained by any page opened, so it is left standing as the Zakarid/Georgian zone ('The realm reached ... Erzurum in the south'). [Repair run 2026-10-31: the Zakarid Armenia page, re-opened, is silent on Georgian control of Erzurum, Karin or any district in modern Turkey around 1210 (Erzurum appears only in a marriage alliance); the +31 k km2 stays unexplained.]
191.2 k km2, unchanged; 'The Zakarids ... governing all of northern Armenia' under Georgian overlordship (Zakarid page). The page says Trebizond (1204) was an ally, not a Georgian dependency.

correction.text: the 1216 outline without Dvin: the Armenian lands under Georgian overlordship stay inside until the Mongols take them in 1239 (Dvin alone is lost to the Khwarazmians in 1226)

keyframe_review.note: Repair run 2026-10-31 (replaces the first correction, Georgia proper plus Ani and Kars, about 75 k km2). Cliopatria's 1227 shape (61.6 k km2, Georgia proper) drops 128 k km2 of Armenian and Erzurum-side land that the 1216 shape (191.2 k km2) held, in one year, with no event but the 40-km Dvin loss. Zakarid Armenia: 'The Zakarids, under Georgian overlordship since 1199-1200'; 'Dvin was lost, but Kars and Ani did not surrender' (1226-1230); 'The Mongols led a major offensive in 1238-39, and took Ani in 1239'; the Georgian kingdom's submission came 'in the 1239 treaty', after which 'the Zakarids ruled not as vassals of the Bagratids, but rather as vassals of the Mongols'. The Mongol page has the 1236 army go against 'Georgia and its vassal Armenian princedoms'. So the 1216 outline minus Dvin stands for 1227-1235 here and, in the new keyframe 1236b, to 1238; the lands leave in 1239 (new ledger entry). Caveat kept open: the Erzurum-side part of the 1216 outline (+31 k km2 from 1210) is itself explained by no page, and Dvin's later fate (back from the Khwarazmians after 1231?) is not on any page; both are listed as gaps. Choice made on the reviewer's advice; the alternative (a dated 1225-26 loss to the Khwarazmians) has no page.

correction.text: the 1216 outline without Dvin, still Georgian (contested by the Mongols) until the 1239 treaty

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1236-1238 inside the 1236 shape: the same correction as 1227 (the 1216 outline without Dvin). Chormaqan went in 1236 'against Georgia and its vassal Armenian princedoms' (Mongol page), Ivane Jaqeli submitted in 1238, and the Zakarid page has Ani taken only 'in 1239'. The fighting is the contest zone of ledger 1236-1243; Georgia proper alone (the 1236 shape) stands from 1239.

61.1 k km2: Georgia proper. Stands for 1239-1240 (after Chormaqan 'conquered Ani and Kars' in 1239 and the Armenian lands became Mongol vassals); for 1236-1238 the new keyframe 1236b holds. [Repair run 2026-10-31.]

correction.text: Georgia proper under Mongol overlordship: 'Georgia officially acknowledged the Great Khan as its overlord' (1243)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Georgian shape for 1241-1332. No page gives the extent of Georgia under the Mongols; the 1236 outline (Georgia proper, 61 k km2) is reused. The kingdom survived: 'In 1256, Georgia was placed under the Mongol empire of the Ilkhanate', the 'Vilayet of Gurjistan' was the Mongol province, and 'Güyük Khan made, in 1247, both pretenders co-kings, in eastern and western parts of the kingdom' (one kingdom, so Imereti is still inside). [Repair run 2026-10-31: years cut from 1241-1329 to 1241-1258.]

correction.text: Georgia proper without Imereti, separated by David Narin's rising

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair run 2026-10-31). No page gives the extent of Georgia under the Mongols; the 1236 outline (Georgia proper, 61 k km2) is reused. 'In 1259-1260, Georgian nobles, led by David Narin, rose against the Mongols' and 'succeeded in separating Imereti (western Georgia) from the Mongol-controlled eastern Georgia' (ledger 1259). The gazetteer's Imereti is the Imereti province (6 k km2), narrower than the page's 'western Georgia'; the rendering agent should expect a small hole.

correction.text: Georgia proper without Imereti and Samtskhe

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair run 2026-10-31). No page gives the extent of Georgia under the Mongols; the 1236 outline (Georgia proper, 61 k km2) is reused. Imereti stays apart (ledger 1259, merged only in 1330) and Samtskhe 'was granted special protection and patronage by Abaqa Khan, thus winning virtual independence from the Georgian crown' (1266; the Samtskhe-Saatabago page: 'seceded and submitted directly to the Ilkhan rule in 1266', infobox 'Vassal of Mongol Empire: 1266-1334'). The double claim of the ilkhanate dossier on this land (1294-1333) is for the orchestrator.

correction.text: the reunited kingdom of 1330 without Samtskhe, which returns only in 1334

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair run 2026-10-31) filling 1330-1332 and taking Samtskhe out of 1333. 'In 1330-31, George V the Brilliant annexed Imereti, uniting all of Georgia in the process' (Mongol page); Klarjeti secured in the 1330s and Armenian lands including Ani held (George V page); but 'In 1334, when his uncle Sargis II Jaqeli, Prince of Samtskhe, died, the king came to Samtskhe' and only then was the reunification complete, so Samtskhe is subtracted. The Cliopatria 1333 shape stands from 1334.

175.9 k km2: George V's reunited kingdom. 'George V essentially completed the process of reunification' in 1334 (Samtskhe); Klarjeti 'secured' in the 1330s; 'Armenian lands, including Ani, were part of the Kingdom of Georgia'. Cliopatria starts a year early, the page gives no frontier. [Repair run 2026-10-31: this shape stands from 1334, when Samtskhe returns (ledger 1334); 1330-1333 is the new keyframe 1330, the same outline without Samtskhe.]
175.2 k km2, a 0.4% change at 1344 that no page explains; George V reigned until 1346 ('George V died in 1346').

163.4 k km2 (-12 k, Erzurum side shrinks). Bagrat V 'inherited the throne' in 1360 and was crowned in Kutaisi 'to mark his rule over western and eastern Georgia'; the page is silent on any loss of land in the 1370s, so the shape is left as drawn (unverified: page budget).
163.5 k km2, unchanged. Timur took Tbilisi on 22 November 1386 and Bagrat V was captured; no border changed in 1385 itself.

correction.text: the 1395 outline plus Kakheti, still part of the kingdom when Timur 'breached the borders' in 1399

keyframe_review.note: 42.0 k km2 is Imereti, Kartli and the north without Kakheti or Samtskhe. 'In the winter of 1399, Timur breached the borders of Kingdom of Georgia' with 'Kakheti and Hereti ... caught by surprise', so Kakheti was still in the kingdom; Samtskhe was invaded in 1386 and 1394 and was brought back only in 1414 (Alexander I page), so it stays out. The Timurid tribute (Cliopatria vassalage 1395-1406) is dated by no page.

correction.text: the 1402 outline plus Kakheti

keyframe_review.note: Same correction as 1395 (44.2 k km2). In 1401 Timur 'made peace with George VII on condition that the King of Georgia supplied him troops'; after the siege of Birtvisi (August 1403) 'Georgia became tributary to the Timurids' and George VII paid '1,000 tankas of gold struck in the name of Timur'. [Repair run 2026-10-31: stands for 1402-1405 and 1410-1414; 1406-1409 is the new keyframe 1406, with Ganja and Nakhchivan.]

correction.text: the 1402 outline plus Kakheti, Ganja and Nakhchivan, which George VII conquered after Timur's death

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1406-1409 inside the 1402 shape. 'He conquered Nakhchivan and Ganja' and George 'succeeded in expanding Georgia's borders temporarily to their former extent' (the sentences follow Timur's death; the 1406 attack is dated on the page). Nakhchivan lies wholly outside Cliopatria's Georgian shapes and Ganja almost wholly; the loss is entered in 1410 at confidence 1 (the page does not date it).

correction.text: the 1415 outline without Lori, which the Kara Koyunlu held until 1431

keyframe_review.note: 127.7 k km2: Samtskhe back ('in 1414, [Alexander] met the rebellious prince Atabeg Ivane Jaqeli of Samtskhe on battlefield and forced him into submission'), Kakheti inside, and the Kars-Ardahan-Artvin-Erzurum side. The outline holds Lori, but 'In 1431, he re-conquered Lori, a Georgian marchland occupied by the Kara Koyunlu', so Lori is taken out until 1431; the Turkish districts are not discussed on any page (unverified: page budget). [Repair run 2026-10-31: the Samtskhe-Saatabago page, opened for this, says of Kars, Ardahan, Artvin, Erzurum and Oltu only that no source there has Samtskhe or Georgia holding them in 1400-1463 (Timur attacked Tao in 1399 and 'set out from Kars' in 1386); the Turkish districts of this outline stay unexplained.]

correction.text: the 1422 outline without Lori until its re-conquest in 1431

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1422-1430 inside the 1422 shape: the 1422 outline without Lori (re-conquered 1431). The 1422 verdict below stands for 1431-1462.

127.8 k km2 stands for 1431-1462 (Lori back). 1433: Alexander made his sons co-rulers 'in Kakheti, Imereti and Kartli'; 1440: Jahan Shah 'sacked the capital city Tbilisi' without annexing; 1442: Alexander abdicated. The page calls him 'the last ruler of a united Georgia'.

correction.text: the Kartli rump plus Kakheti, where George VIII reigned, until the kingdom of Kakheti emerges in 1466

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1463-1465 (repair run 2026-10-31). After Chikhori (1463) the crown still holds Kartli and Kakheti; Kakheti page: the kingdom 'emerged in the process of a tripartite division of the Kingdom of Georgia in 1466', George VIII having been captured 'in 1465'. Without this keyframe Kakheti would belong to no state on the map in 1463-1465. Imereti and Samtskhe stand apart from 1463 (ledger 1463). The page gives no extent (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: the Kartli rump of the Georgian kingdom after Kakheti's separation, shown as Cliopatria's 1468 outline

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1466-1467 (renamed from 1463; repair run 2026-10-31). Once Kakheti is a kingdom (1466, Kakheti page) the Georgian crown holds only Kartli: 'Bagrat VI ... proclaimed himself King of all Georgia in 1466' and 'continued to rule Kartli until 1478'; the 1468 outline (27.6 k km2) is used. The page gives no extent (unverified: page budget).

27.6 k km2: Kartli. Stands for 1468-1477 as the rump of the Georgian kingdom (Bagrat VI, 'King of all Georgia' from 1466; 'Constantine established himself as a de facto ruler over part of Kartli in 1469'). correction.text: the same Cliopatria outline, filed under the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti (1762-1801)

union.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

region.text: Bagrat III's Georgia: the 1010 outline without Kakheti-Hereti and Tbilisi

ledger.note: 1008: Bagrat III unites the Georgian lands. Infobox 'Unification: c. 1008'; 'Gurgen died in 1008, leaving his throne for Bagrat'; in 978 the aristocracy 'invited Bagrat to claim the throne of Abkhazia'. Capital Kutaisi. The page gives no frontier; Cliopatria's first shape is dated 1010.

region.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

ledger.note: 1010: Bagrat III annexes Kakheti-Hereti. 'Bagrat ... annexed it in 1010'; the region is independent again in George I's first year (1014).

region.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

ledger.note: 1014: George I recognises Kakheti-Hereti's independence. 'In an agreement that deprived Georgia of more than a third of its territory within the first year of his reign, he recognized the independence of Kakheti'; Kvirike III 'assumed the title of King of Kakheti and Hereti'. Bagrat III died on 7 May 1014; the page gives no month for the agreement.

region.text: Tao and the neighbouring Byzantine-Georgian marches (Tao, Shavsheti, Artaani, Kola, the plains of Basiani)

ledger.note: 1015: George I invades Tao. 'George I invaded the disputed territory for the first time in 1015 or 1016, without provoking an immediate military response from the emperor' (Kingdom of Georgia page: 'occupied Tao starting from 1015 or 1016').

region.text: Tao and the neighbouring Byzantine-Georgian marches (Tao, Shavsheti, Artaani, Kola, the plains of Basiani)

ledger.note: 1023: Georgia gives up Tao to Basil II. Shirimni was fought on 11 September 1021 ('narrowly won by Basil II's troops'); 'During the winter of 1022-1023, he seized the opportunity to reoccupy Tao'; the treaty came 'soon afterward' and the page does not date it: 'Georgia lost control over Tao, Javakheti, Shavsheti, the plains of Basiani, and the towns of Artaani and Kola'.

1023: Javakheti passes to Byzantium. 'Georgia was also compelled to cede fourteen fortresses and to renounce all claims to the territories of David Kuropalates'; Javakheti is the only one of the ceded lands inside Cliopatria's outline. Second page (Basil II, opened 2026-10-31): 'George agreed to a treaty that handed over Tao, Phasiane, Kola, Artaan and Javakheti'; the sentence carries no year. Keyframes 1023, 1046 and 1072 now subtract this circle until Cliopatria's 1099 shape.

1080: the emir Ahmed takes Kutaisi. 'Since 1080, when the emir Ahmed captured Kutaisi', Georgia accepted Seljuk suzerainty and an annual tribute (Seljuk wars page: 'from 1079/80 onward, George was pressured into submitting to Malik-Shah'; Kartli and Argveti pillaged in 1068). Cliopatria draws the loss in 1085.

1099: David IV stops paying tribute and the lowlands come back. 'enabled David IV to cease paying tribute to the Seljuks in 1099'; no page dates the recovery of Kutaisi or Kartli (the first dated battle is Trialeti in 1110), so the region is Cliopatria's 1099 shape; page silent.

1099: Javakheti is Georgian again (bridging entry, page silent on the year). Javakheti page: 'This territory suffered greatly from the invasions of Alp Arslan in 1064' and it 'remained in the hands of the unified Georgian monarchy' in later centuries; no opened page (Javakheti, Bagrat IV, Basil II, David IV, Georgian-Seljuk wars) dates the return. The date and the Seljuk counterpart rest on Cliopatria drawing the circle outside the 1085-1098 shape and inside the 1099 shape.

region.text: Kakheti-Hereti: Kakheti and, east of it, Hereti (read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki)

ledger.note: 1104: David IV annexes Kakheti-Hereti. 'In 1104, a conspiracy led by the Heretian nobles' handed Aghsartan II to David and 'the citadels and fortresses of Kakheti surrendered without resistance'; Arishiani was appointed governor.
1115: Rustavi is retaken. 'In 1115, George of Chqondidi captured Rustavi, one of the strong Turkish strongholds in southern Georgia.'

1118: David IV takes Lori and Agarak. 'Still in 1118, the Armenian towns of Lori and Agarak were captured by David IV'; the page does not name the previous holder; kingdom-of-tashir-dzoraget, which the bagratid-armenia dossier lists as its successor holding Lori, is a guess.

February 1122: David IV retakes Tbilisi. 'Already in June 1121, David IV had besieged the city of Tbilisi' and 'took the city in February'; Didgori was won on 12 August 1121 and Tbilisi is 'the last Muslim enclave remaining from the Seljuk occupation, in 1122' (Seljuk wars page).
1122: the capital moves from Kutaisi to Tbilisi. 'the king transferred the capital from Kutaisi to Tbilisi' after the capture; infobox 'Tbilisi (c. 1122-1490)'.

June 1123: David IV invades Shirvan. 'In June 1123, a month after the defeat of the Seljuks, David IV invaded Shirvan.' Gishi had been taken in 1117 and Manuchihr III replaced by David's son-in-law in 1120.

March 1124: Dmanisi falls. 'In March 1124, he managed to attack the last Muslim stronghold in Georgia, Dmanisi, which he took after a short fight.' The pages disagree: the Kingdom of Georgia page has 'In 1123, David IV liberated Dmanisi' and the Demetrius page has Demetrius 'expel the Seljuks from the fortress of Dmanisi' in 1125.

August 1124: Ani opens its gates to David IV. Representatives came 'to David IV on August 20, 1124'; 'Without a single fight, the Armenian population of Ani opened the gates to the Georgians'; 'Northern Armenia was thus annexed and incorporated into the Kingdom of Georgia'. The holder is not named on this page; the Shaddadids are read from the Demetrius and Zakarid pages.

September 1124: Shamakhi is recovered. 'Another military campaign was organized in September in Shirvan ... [David] managed to recover Shamakhi' (the year comes from the paragraph); Kingdom of Georgia page: 'By 1124, Shirvan was captured along with the Armenian city of Ani'.

1130: the Shirvan war ends on the Tetritsqali. In 1129-30 'the Christian part was incorporated into Georgia and the border being the Tetritsqali'; in 1125 Manuchihr had 'regained control of western Shirvan' and in 1126 'the Muslim population of Shirvan rebelled with the support of the Seljuks'.

region.text: Shirvan east of the Tetritsqali border: the part of the 1126 outline that the 1139 outline no longer has

ledger.note: 1130: eastern Shirvan leaves the Georgian outline. 'The Christian part was incorporated into Georgia and the border being the Tetritsqali' and 'Manuchihr was appointed as the emir of eastern Shirvan and recognized Georgia's vassalage' (both 1129-30): the land east of the border becomes a vassal (next entry) and is no longer Georgia's own. Keyframe 1130 draws it. The shirvan dossier records the matching gain in 1130.

1130: Ani is given up. 'In 1130, the ruler of the Shah-Armens launched an attempt to oust Georgians from northern and central Armenia' and 'Demetrius had to come to terms and give up Ani to the Shaddadids on terms of vassalage'. The vassal entry follows; the shaddadids dossier records its own 1125 gain.

region.text: eastern Shirvan under Manuchihr, east of the Tetritsqali border

ledger.note: 1130: eastern Shirvan becomes a Georgian vassal. Manuchihr was made 'emir of eastern Shirvan' and 'recognized Georgia's vassalage'.
1130: Ani goes to the Shaddadids as a vassal. 'Demetrius had to come to terms and give up Ani to the Shaddadids on terms of vassalage.'
1161: George III ends the Shaddadid hold on Ani. 'In 1161, George III took over Ani.'
1161: George III takes over Ani (Seljuk wars page: 'In July, 1161 troops of a Muslim coalition' attacked it).
April 1164: Georgia evacuates Ani. 'On 9 July 1163 Seljuks inflicted a heavy defeat on Georgians' and 'In April, 1164 Georgians evacuated the town'; the page does not name the taker.
1174: George III takes Ani again. 'In 1174 King George captured the Shahanshah ibn Mahmud as a prisoner and captured Ani once again.'

1175: bridging entry, page silent. Ani is back under Shaddadid control by 1199 ('took the city of Ani from Shadaddid control'); 'Ani would be captured five times between 1124 and 1209'; the year of the loss is not given.

1190: bridging entry, page silent. The Tamar page has Georgia only 'Early in the 1190s ... began to interfere' with the Shirvanshahs, so the 1130 vassalage had lapsed before; the year is a placeholder.

Early 1190s: Shirvan becomes a tributary again. 'Early in the 1190s, the Georgian government began to interfere in the affairs of the Eldiguzids and of the Shirvanshahs' ... 'reducing Shirvan to a tributary state'; 1195: the Eldiguzid atabeg 'lost his capital to a Georgian protege' after Shamkor.

1199: Zakare retakes Ani for Georgia. 'Around the year 1199, a Georgian army under Zakare's command took the city of Ani from Shadaddid control' and 'in 1201, Tamar gave it to him as a fief': 'Under Georgian overlordship since 1199-1200'.

ledger.counterpart: Dvin's Muslim holders (the page does not name them)
ledger.note: 1203-1205: Georgians seize Dvin. 'between 1203 and 1205 Georgians seized the town of Dvin'; the year is the start of the span.
1206: David Soslan takes Kars. 'In 1206, the Georgian army, under the command of David Soslan, captured Kars and other fortresses', after 'the ruler of Erzerum refused to submit to Georgia'.

1225: Jalal ad-Din attacks Georgia. 'That same year, he attacked Georgia, defeating its forces in the battle of Garni' (after setting himself up in Tabriz on 25 July 1225). This page dates the capture of Tbilisi to 1225; the Mongol invasions page says 'Tbilisi was captured in 1226'.
1225: bridging entry, page silent. Georgian overlordship over Shirvan ends with the Khwarazmian conquest of Azerbaijan (Tabriz, July 1225); no page opened dates the end.
1226: Dvin is lost to the Khwarazmians. 'In 1226-1230, Dvin was lost, but Kars and Ani did not surrender.'
15 August 1231: Jalal ad-Din is killed. 'Eventually, he was killed in 15 August 1231.' The page is silent on when the Khwarazmian garrisons left Georgia.

region.text: Georgia and its vassal Armenian princedoms

ledger.note: 1236: Chormaqan invades Georgia. 'The third and final invasion of the Caucasus by the Mongols took place in 1236'; he 'led, in 1236, a large army against Georgia and its vassal Armenian princedoms'; Ivane Jaqeli submitted in 1238. The first Mongol contact was in the fall of 1220, the return in force in January 1221.
1236: bridging entry. 'Queen Rusudan had to evacuate Tbilisi for Kutaisi'; the page places this in the 1236-1243 conquest and gives no year.
1239: the Mongols take Ani and Kars. 'In 1239, Chormaqan conquered Ani and Kars in Greater Armenia.'

region.text: the Armenian princedoms and Erzurum-side lands of the 1216 outline outside Georgia proper (Ani and Kars are the entry above)

ledger.note: 1239: the Armenian princedoms pass to the Mongols. 'The Mongols led a major offensive in 1238-39, and took Ani in 1239'; the Georgian kingdom submitted 'in the 1239 treaty' and 'the Zakarids ruled not as vassals of the Bagratids, but rather as vassals of the Mongols'. The year is the page's, the region is the reading of the 1216 outline outside the 1236 outline (Cliopatria's 1227 and 1236 shapes drop it); the page says nothing about the Erzurum-side districts, which are carried with them (unexplained since 1210).

1243: Georgia submits to the Great Khan. 'Atabeg Avag arranged her submission in 1243, and Georgia officially acknowledged the Great Khan as its overlord'; tribute of '50,000 gold pieces' and an army. The vassal tint belongs to the Mongol Empire's and Ilkhanate's dossiers (counterpart kingdom-of-georgia).

1259-1260: David VI Narin's revolt separates western Georgia. 'In 1259–1260, Georgian nobles, led by David Narin, rose against the Mongols' and 'succeeded in separating Imereti (western Georgia) from the Mongol-controlled eastern Georgia'. The 1247 arrangement ('Güyük Khan made, in 1247, both pretenders co-kings, in eastern and western parts of the kingdom respectively') was a co-kingship within one kingdom, not a split. [Reviewer eu-19-d, 2026-10-31: year moved from 1247 to 1259 on the same page.]

1266: Samtskhe wins virtual independence. It 'was granted special protection and patronage by Abaqa Khan, thus winning virtual independence from the Georgian crown' (dated 1266 by the page's account).

1327: George V begins to free Georgia from the Ilkhanate. In 1327 Abu Sa'id executed his guardian; 'It was a long process that lasted from 1327 to 1335, through both peaceful diplomacy and the use of force'; 'He stopped paying tribute to the Mongols and expelled their army from the country'.
1330: George V annexes Imereti and reunites Georgia. 'In 1330-31, George V the Brilliant annexed Imereti, uniting all of Georgia in the process' (infobox 'Reunification: 1329').

region.text: the part of the 1333 outline outside modern Georgia: Klarjeti, Ani and the Armenian lands

ledger.note: 1330s: bridging entry, year not given. 'In the 1330s, George secured the southwestern province of Klarjeti against the advancing Osmanli tribesmen' and 'During his reign, Armenian lands, including Ani, were part of the Kingdom of Georgia'; Cliopatria's large 1333 outline is the only dated trace.

1334: Samtskhe returns to the crown. 'In 1334, when his uncle Sargis II Jaqeli, Prince of Samtskhe, died, the king came to Samtskhe'; 'With this act, George V essentially completed the process of reunification of Georgia.'
1335: the Ilkhanate collapses. The 1327-1335 'process' ends as the 'Ilkhanate was divided into several neighboring states'; Il-Khanid coins were still minted in Tiflis until the 1350s.

1357: the Jalayirids occupy Tiflis. 'The Jalayirids occupied the Georgian capital Tiflis in 1357-1358,' where they minted coins in Shaykh Uways's name; hatched, not annexed. The same page has Jani Beg of the Golden Horde: 'Jani Beg occupied the Georgian capital of Tiflis in 1356, and issued his own coinage there' (not entered: golden-horde dossier, group ia-02). The jalayirid-sultanate dossier records the same event with the roles reversed.
1358: Tiflis is left (the occupation lasted 1357-1358 on the page).
22 November 1386: Timur takes Tbilisi. '[Tbilisi] fell on 22 November 1386, its inhabitants were massacred and Bagrat fell into captivity' (Bagrat V page: captured 'after a six-month siege').
1387: Alexander is crowned king of Imereti. 'in 1387 [Alexander] was crowned king of Imereti in Gelati monastery' after he 'proclaimed himself an independent ruler'.
1389: Bagrat V restores his suzerainty over Imereti. 'In 1389, after the death of the Imeretian king Alexander, Bagrat V managed to restore his suzerainty over his successor.'

region.text: the southern, Armenian and Turkish lands of the 1394 outline, including Samtskhe

ledger.note: 1395: bridging entry, the page does not say what Georgia lost. 'In the spring of 1394, he came to southern Georgia and sent four commanders with an army of 40,000'; Samtskhe (Akhaltsikhe, Kors, Kola) was invaded in 1386 and 1394; Timur gave the lands 'from Beylagan to Trebizond' to Khalil Mirza. Cliopatria shrinks the outline in 1395.

August 1403: Birtvisi falls and Georgia becomes Timur's tributary. 'Having captured the fortress in August 1403, Timur sent his army to plunder'; 'Georgia became tributary to the Timurids' (undated); George VII kept independence as a Christian kingdom and paid '1,000 tankas of gold struck in the name of Timur'. Cliopatria dates the vassalage 1395-1406.

1406: George VII retakes Nakhchivan and Ganja. After Timur's death George 'engaged in battles to regain lost territories, conquering Nakhchivan and Ganja'; 'In 1406, George suddenly attacked and drove the enemy towards Tabriz' with 'merely 5,000 men' and 'temporarily restored Georgia's former borders'.

1410: Ganja and Nakhchivan are lost again (bridging entry; the Timur page does not say when or how, and does not mention the Qara Qoyunlu). Bounds from the Qara Qoyunlu page: Qara Yusuf 'defeated the Timurid Abu Bakr at the Battle of Nakhchivan' (14 October 1406), 'They started the Turkoman invasions of Georgia (1407-1502)', and 'In 1410, Armenia fell under the control of the Qara Qoyunlu'. The page names Ganja and Nakhchivan only as tribal locations.
1414: Alexander I subdues Samtskhe. 'in 1414, [he] met the rebellious prince Atabeg Ivane Jaqeli of Samtskhe on battlefield and forced him into submission.'
1431: Alexander I retakes Lori. 'In 1431, he re-conquered Lori, a Georgian marchland occupied by the Kara Koyunlu.'

1463: Chikhori breaks the kingdom. 'Major disintegration of the Georgian kingdom dates from 1463 with the defeat of George VIII at the Battle of Chikhori'; the page dates Imereti's own king to 1484 ('Alexander, proclaimed himself king of Imereti (Western Georgia)'), the kingdom-of-imereti dossier founds it in 1463.

1463: Samtskhe stands apart. The page has Constantine 'subordinate Samtskhe' only in 1481, so it was outside the Kartli rump before; it had been 'virtually independent' since 1266 (Mongol invasions page) and was only briefly brought back in 1334 and 1414.

minus.text: the Kartli rump, Imereti, Kakheti and Samtskhe

region.text: the rest of the 1422 outline: Abkhazia and the northern marches, Klarjeti, Ani and Kars, Lori, Ganja and Nakhchivan

ledger.note: 1463: bridging entry, page silent. These lands are outside Cliopatria's 1468 outlines; the page names no taker (the seed's neighbours for 1463-1467 are the Ottoman Empire, Qara Qoyunlu, Shirvan and the Timurids).

region.text: Kakheti, where George VIII reigned after Chikhori

ledger.note: 1466: Kakheti becomes a kingdom. Kakheti page: 'It emerged in the process of a tripartite division of the Kingdom of Georgia in 1466', after George VIII 'was captured by his defiant vassal Qvarqvare III Jaqeli, Duke of Samtskhe, in 1465'. The Kartli page has George VIII defeated at Chikhori in 1463 and captured in 1465 and does not date the Kakheti kingdom (the page does not mention 1463 on the Kakheti side). Until 1466 Kakheti stays inside the Kartli rump (keyframe 1463). [Repair run 2026-10-31: moved from 1463 to 1466 to agree with the kingdom-of-kakheti dossier.]

1478: the Georgian kingdom is divided in three. Kartli 'emerged in the process of a tripartite division of the Kingdom of Georgia in 1478' (infobox 'Established: 1478'); Bagrat VI 'continued to rule Kartli until 1478'. The Kingdom of Georgia page ends it 'De facto 1463', 'De jure 1490' ('In 1490, Constantine II summoned a special royal council that recognized the fragmentation'). The map ends this state in 1478, when the Kartli dossier takes the land over.

wars.name: Georgian-Byzantine war over Tao

zones.text: Tao and the neighbouring Byzantine-Georgian marches (Tao, Shavsheti, Artaani, Kola, the plains of Basiani)

wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: Basil II won at Shirimni on 11 September 1021; after the winter of 1022-1023 George I lost Tao, Javakheti, Shavsheti, the plains of Basiani, Artaani and Kola and fourteen fortresses.
wars.note: The treaty is undated on the page ('soon afterward' after the winter of 1022-1023), so 1023 is the earliest year that fits.

wars.name: Seljuk invasions of Georgia
wars.outcome: Alp Arslan came in 1064 and 1068 (Bagrat had to leave Kakheti for Kartli), Malik-Shah in 1076; from 1079/80 George II paid an annual tribute; the emir Ahmed took Kutaisi in 1080 (David IV page).
wars.note: The Great Turkish Invasion: 'the Seljuq garrisons occupied the key fortresses in Georgia's south'; a disastrous earthquake struck in 1088.

wars.name: Georgian reconquest from the Seljuks
wars.outcome: Georgian victory: no tribute from 1099; Trialeti 1110, Rustavi 1115, Lori 1118, Botora (February 1120), Didgori (12 August 1121), Tbilisi (February 1122), Dmanisi (March 1124).

wars.name: Georgian-Shirvan war
wars.outcome: David IV invaded in June 1123 and recovered Shamakhi in September 1124; after Manuchihr's return (1125) and a rebellion (1126) Demetrius settled in 1129-30 on a border at the Tetritsqali, eastern Shirvan under Manuchihr as Georgian vassal.
wars.note: The Shirvan dossier (this group) records the same 1123-1124 campaign from the other side.

wars.name: Wars for Ani
wars.outcome: Ani passed from the Shaddadids to David IV (1124), back to them as a vassal (1130), to George III (1161), out (1164), in again (1174) and finally to Zakare for Georgia (c. 1199); 'Ani would be captured five times between 1124 and 1209'.
wars.note: Saltuk II marched on Ani in 1153-54 and was captured by Demetrius (Demetrius page).

wars.name: Tamar's wars against the Eldiguzids, Rum and Erzurum
wars.outcome: Georgian gains: Shirvan tributary (early 1190s), Shamkor (1195), Basian (1202, 1203 or 1204), Dvin (1203-1205), Kars (1206); in 1209 Georgia besieged Khlat and raided Ardabil, Marand, Tabriz and Qazvin without annexing.
wars.note: The Trebizond founders (1204) were Tamar's allies, not vassals.

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Georgia
wars.outcome: Jalal ad-Din beat the Georgians at Garni (1225) and took Tbilisi (1225 on this page, 1226 on the Mongol page); Dvin was lost in 1226-1230 while Ani and Kars held; he was killed on 15 August 1231.
wars.note: Thin page: it names no Georgian territorial loss.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Georgia

zones.text: Georgia and its vassal Armenian princedoms

wars.outcome: The raids of 1220-1221 were followed by the conquest of 1236-1243: Ivane submitted in 1238, Ani and Kars fell in 1239, Georgia acknowledged the Great Khan in 1243 and paid tribute.

wars.name: Georgian rebellion against the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: Georgian nobles under David Narin rose in 1259-1260; the page gives no outcome and no territorial change.

wars.name: George V's liberation from Ilkhanid rule
wars.outcome: Georgia stopped paying tribute and expelled the Mongol army between 1327 and 1335; the Mongols mounted further campaigns in the 1330s and 1340s 'with no success'.
wars.note: Coins suggest Tiflis stayed Il-Khanid into the 1350s; the page notes the evidence is disputed.

wars.name: Timur's invasions of Georgia
wars.outcome: Timur took Tbilisi on 22 November 1386, returned in 1387, 1388, 1394, 1399, 1400 and 1401 and captured Birtvisi in August 1403; Georgia became his tributary but kept its independence, and George VII regained Nakhchivan and Ganja in 1406 (lost again by 1410 on the evidence of the Qara Qoyunlu page, confidence 1).

wars.name: Reconquest of Lori
wars.outcome: Alexander I re-conquered Lori 'from the Turkomans' in 1431; c. 1434/5 he granted it under vassalage to the Armenian prince Beshken II Orbelian.

wars.name: Jahan Shah's invasion of Georgia
wars.outcome: After Alexander refused tribute, Jahan Shah destroyed Samshvilde and sacked Tbilisi in March 1440; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Collapse of the kingdom: Chikhori to the tripartite division
wars.outcome: George VIII was beaten at Chikhori (1463) and captured (1465); Bagrat VI proclaimed himself king of all Georgia in 1466; the realm divided into Kartli (1478), Imereti and Kakheti, with the de jure end in 1490.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Georgia page adds Uzun Hasan's attacks in 1466, 1472 and possibly 1476-77.

certainty.note: Medieval frontiers are described by cities and provinces, not lines; the only fixed line on the pages is the Tetritsqali border in Shirvan from 1129-30. The Mongol-period extent (1241-1329) has no page at all.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (39 shapes, 1010..1802) is three states. This dossier is the united Kingdom of Georgia, 1008-1478 (Cliopatria shapes 1010..1468 plus new keyframes: 1008, 1010b, 1023, 1130, 1236b, 1241, 1259, 1266, 1330, 1406, 1422b, 1463, 1466; repair run of 2026-10-31). The end year is the tripartite division of 1478 (Kartli page); the kingdom's own page gives 1463 (de facto, Chikhori) and 1490 (de jure), and the Imereti dossier founds Imereti in 1463. The eight shapes 1507..1578 and 1706..1762 are the Kingdom of Kartli (verdict wrong here; the kingdom-of-kartli dossier of another part of eu-19 already carries them, starting in 1478; the 1468 shape serves this dossier for 1468-1477; Cliopatria's own Kingdom of Kartli row covers only 1463-1467, rejected there, and 1612-1705) and the five shapes 1763..1802 are the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, written in this batch as kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti. Keyframe convention used: a new keyframe whose years lie inside a Cliopatria shape's span (1010b, 1023, 1130, 1236b, 1330, 1406, 1422b) overrides that shape in those years; the shape's own verdict says which years it then stands for. Main corrections to Cliopatria: Kakheti-Hereti and Tbilisi are not Georgian in 1014-1103/1122 (shapes 1010, 1046, 1072 are about all of modern Georgia); the 1126 outline holds Ani and eastern Shirvan only to 1129; the 1227 outline (Georgia proper only, 61.6 k km2 against 191.2 k km2 in 1216) wrongly drops the Armenian lands, kept here (1216 outline minus Dvin) until the 1239 treaty; the 1395-1414 outline omits Kakheti; the 1415 and 1422 outlines hold Lori before its 1431 re-conquest; no shape exists for 1241-1332 (the kingdom lived on under the Mongols) or for 1008-1009. Unexplained Cliopatria changes left as drawn: 1210 (+31 k km2 into Turkey; the Zakarid page, re-opened, is silent), 1344, 1375 (-12 k km2 at Erzurum), 1385; the Erzurum-side part of the 1216-1238 outline rests on that unexplained 1210 jump, and the 1415 Turkish districts on none. Conflicts between pages: Tbilisi taken by Jalal ad-Din in 1225 (Jalal page) or 1226 (Mongol page); Dmanisi 1123 (Kingdom page), March 1124 (David IV page), 1125 (Demetrius page); Basian 1202, 1203 or 1204; end of the kingdom 1463 (Chikhori, infobox de facto), 1466 (Kingdom page lead), 1478 (Kartli page), 1490 (infobox de jure); reunification 1329 (infobox), 1330-31 (Mongol page), 1334 (George V page). Pages that failed or were thin: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalal_al-Din_Mingburnu (url_not_found, replaced by Jalal_ad-Din_Mingburnu, which is thin); Bagrat V and Tamar pages silent on losses and Ani 1199. All 14 pages of the budget are used; the Georgia-Armenia-Shirvan detail of the 1124-1130 years rests on the David IV and Demetrius pages alone. Not collected: the ruler strip (the pages give fragments, no full list; a gap-filler should open 'List of monarchs of Georgia'); Bagrat III, Bagrat IV, George II, Constantine I and Vakhtang IV have no page; Samtskhe, Imereti and Abkhazia relations before 1463 are only as the pages give them. Conf-1 events (bridging, page silent): 1099 recovery of the lowlands, 1175 loss of Ani, 1190 and 1225 vassal ends for Shirvan, 1236 move to Kutaisi, 1330s Klarjeti and Armenian lands, 1395 loss to Timur. Counterparts that need dossiers: kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti (1010-1105), shaddadids (Ani, Dvin and Ganja branches), saltukids (Erzurum), eldiguzids, kingdom-of-abkhazia (to 1008), kingdom-of-tashir-dzoraget (Lori, to 1118; named in bagratid-armenia's successors). Counterparts with a row elsewhere: byzantine-empire, great-seljuk-empire, shirvan, mongol-empire, ilkhanate, timurid-empire, qara-qoyunlu, khwarezmid-empire, kingdom-of-imereti, samtskhe-saatabago, kingdom-of-kartli, sultanate-of-rum, ayyubid-sultanate. The vassal tints of Georgia under the Great Khan (1243-1327) and Timur (1395-1406) belong in the suzerains' dossiers with counterpart kingdom-of-georgia. Region names the gazetteer lacks: Tao, Klarjeti, Hereti, Kakheti-Hereti, Tbilisi emirate (regions); Dmanisi, Dvin, Akhalkalaki, Shamakhi, Gori, Akhaltsikhe, Telavi (places, replaced by coordinates or admin-1 here). REPAIR RUN 2026-10-31 (after the adversarial review): (1) ledger 1259 Imereti split re-dated from 1247 by the reviewer (kept); the 1241-1329 keyframe is split into 1241, 1259, 1266 and 1330 so that Imereti (1259-1330) and Samtskhe (1266-1334) are out of the outline in their years and 1330-1332 is covered. (2) 1227: the 1216 outline minus Dvin stands to 1238 (keyframes 1227, 1236b) and a 1239 loss to the Mongols takes the rest; the choice follows the reviewer, with the doubt that the Erzurum-side third of that outline is explained by no page. (3) Kakheti's split moved to 1466 (Kakheti page) with a keyframe 1463-1465 that keeps Kakheti inside; the 1468 outline alone from 1466. (4) Two 1130 losses (Shirvan east of the Tetritsqali; Ani) added before the vassal entries; about half of the 1126-to-1139 area difference stays without a page event. (5) The 1406 gain of Ganja and Nakhchivan now shows in keyframe 1406 (1406-1409) and ends in a confidence-1 loss in 1410 to qara-qoyunlu (the Timur page does not date it). (6) Javakheti is subtracted from 1023 (keyframes 1023, 1046, 1072) and returns, confidence 1, in 1099 where Cliopatria draws it again. (7) Occupation of Tiflis by the Jalayirids, 1357-1358, added. Counterpart slugs outside their dossiers' lives: kingdom-of-imereti (dossier 1463-1810) stands in for the western Georgian kingdom of 1259-1330 (ledger 1259, 1330) and for Imereti in 1387-1389; samtskhe-saatabago (Cliopatria 1468-1506) stands in for the Samtskhe principality from 1266 (ledger 1266, 1334, 1414, 1463); their owners (eu-19) or the orchestrator should extend those dossiers or give them earlier slugs. Disagreements with the review: none on dates; on the Imereti region, the gazetteer's Imereti is the province (6 k km2) while the Mongol page means 'western Georgia'; I kept {region: Imereti} as ledger 1259 does. The reviewer's 1410 date for the loss of Ganja and Nakhchivan is a bridge only (no page). Pages opened in the repair run: Mongol invasions, Zakarid Armenia, Demetrius I, Timur's invasions (re-opened); Kingdom of Kakheti, Jalayirid Sultanate, Qara Qoyunlu, Basil II, Javakheti, Bagrat IV, Samtskhe-Saatabago (new); this goes beyond the 14-page budget of the original brief by seven pages, each needed for one finding.
